summary: R1.1 candidate: static red-team review found no direct self-approval without a valid, unredeemed invite in a paired atomic batch. Score is provisional: Firebase Rules Emulator and a diff against actual Published Firestore/Storage Rules have not been completed. DO NOT PUBLISH YET.

findings.issue: Issuing invitations requires an existing Firebase custom claim admin:true, whose presence for the owner has not been independently verified.
findings.recommendation: Verify the owner's ID token custom claim through a trusted channel before enabling invite generation. Do not trust profiles_v2.role.

findings.check: Atomic counter/action replay and update bypass
findings.issue: Both halves of one-time redemption are cross-checked using getAfter(), but correctness and Firestore Rules syntax have only been structurally tested, not by the Firebase Emulator.
findings.recommendation: Test fresh, expired, revoked, reused, simultaneous, forged and one-sided batch writes in Emulator before any Publish.

findings.check: Business logic versus Rules and mixed-content leak
findings.issue: Public Web uses one entire Firestore document, and actual Published Rules/data are not yet inspected. Older EPUB or private fields mixed into main_library would remain public.
findings.recommendation: Read-only audit the live main_library document and compare the complete Published Firestore/Storage Rules before rollout.

findings.issue: Firestore Rules deny new server reads after revocation but cannot retroactively erase previously downloaded or offline-cached content. UI gates are staged off.
findings.recommendation: Exercise logout/account switch and cache behavior on Android and laptop; activate client flags only after server policy is live.

findings.issue: The pre-existing profile contains self-mutable virtual Xu; invitation rules do not provide a validated payment entitlement or strong anti-cheat controls.
findings.recommendation: Keep all real-value transactions and paid EPUB entitlement authorization separate; no additional anti-cheat changes are needed for the owner's current solo-play scope.
